headlines.article_text: LIV Golf faces liquidation after BC Partners scraps rescue plan Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points BC Partners dropped a plan to finance up to $300 million for a revamped LIV Golf after the league failed to secure enough player commitments. LIV Golf is in Chapter 11 and is scheduled to appear in U.S. bankruptcy court Thursday. The outcome of the hearing and the league’s ultimate fate remain unclear. Saudi Arabia’s PIF said it would stop funding LIV after the 2026 season in September. A general view of the 18th hole during day four of LIV Golf Indianapolis at The Club at Chatham Hills on Aug. 23, 2026 in Westfield, Indiana. Michael Miller | ISI Photos | Getty Images LIV Golf could be headed for liquidation after BC Partners Credit reportedly dropped plans to finance a relaunch of the breakaway league. The investment firm had pledged up to $300 million for a revamped version of LIV, known as LIV 2.0, but withdrew the plan after LIV Golf failed to secure enough player commitments, according to the Associated Press. LIV is scheduled to appear in U.S. bankruptcy court Thursday, with the hearing now expected to focus on liquidation of its assets. The league's ultimate fate remains unclear. LIV Golf and BC Partners did not immediately respond to CNBC's requests for comment. LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund said it would stop funding the league after the 2026 season. PIF had invested more than $5 billion since LIV launched in 2022, according to its Chapter 11 filing. BC Partners' proposed relaunch would have made players majority owners of the reorganized league and featured a scaled-back schedule. But LIV has lost several prominent players, including Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia, as it sought commitments for the new venture. Rahm said Tuesday that uncertainty over the league's future and proposed changes to its format influenced his decision to leave. "There were too many unknowns at the time, and there's still quite a few," he told reporters ahead of the Abu Dhabi Championship. Rahm added that the revamped competition appeared to be moving away from the team format that initially attracted him. Garcia, who secured a release from his LIV contract in October, has outlined plans to return to the DP World Tour and explore a possible return to the PGA Tour. Only four players had publicly committed to LIV 2.0: Richard Bland, Cameron Tringale, Brendan Steele and Ben Campbell, according to Golf Digest. LIV launched in 2022 as a challenger to the PGA Tour, recruiting prominent players including Phil Mickelson, Dustin Johnson and Bryson DeChambeau with lucrative contracts. Its arrival split men's professional golf, with the PGA Tour suspending members who competed in LIV events. The disputes later spilled into the courts, with players challenging suspensions and the rival organizations pursuing competing legal claims. The PGA Tour denied the allegations , while LIV dismissed the counterclaims. A June 2023 framework agreement between the PGA Tour, DP World Tour and PIF ended their litigation and proposed combining their commercial businesses, although the deal was never completed. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Snap shares sank over 10% when the Snapchat parent missed on revenue and daily active users in its third-quarter earnings report Wednesday. Here's how the company did compared with analysts' expectations: Earnings per share : $0.19 adj. vs. $0.16 expected, according to LSEG Revenue : $1.72 billion vs. $1.73 billion expected, according to LSEG Global daily active users : 495 million vs. 499 million expected, according to StreetAccount Global average revenue per user, or ARPU : $3.48 vs. $3.48 expected, according to StreetAccount Sales in Snap's third quarter jumped 14% year-over-year while net income came in at $56 million, compared to the $104 million net loss it logged the prior year. Snap's third-quarter adjusted earnings came in at $383 million, topping the $337 million that analysts were projecting, according to StreetAccount. The Snapchat parent said fourth-quarter revenue should come in between $1.95 billion and $1.99 billion. The midpoint of that figure is higher than Wall Street's estimates of $1.95 billion. Fourth-quarter adjusted earnings are expected to come in between $490 million and $525 million. Analysts were expecting that figure to be $498 million. Snap executives said in an investor letter that the company plans for globally monthly active users to become its "primary audience metric" starting in its first quarter for 2027. The company also said it has 977 MAU for the quarter. "Daily engagement has historically been stable as a percentage of monthly engagement, but we do not intend to optimize Snapchat around daily use at the expense of long-term value for our community," the investor letter said. "A longer-term horizon better aligns our reported metrics with the product and safety decisions that strengthen relationships, create lasting utility, and support broader, more durable audience growth." Snap chief commercial officer Ronan Harris told analysts during an earnings call that lower spending by unspecified consumer packaged goods, or CPG, companies impacted third-quarter sales. Harris attributed the curbed CPG spending to "macro pressures in the U.S. and also the Middle East." "As we look ahead, we're seeing very positive signs of growth from diversified verticals like financial services in the U.S.," Harris said.
